walkthroughs.body_html:
Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Dialogue Between Religious & Non-Religious Beliefs — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Dialogue Between Religious & Non-Religious Beliefs brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Dialogue Between Religious & Non-Religious Beliefs.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.

mcqs.q: What does Buddhism teach about suffering?
options: All existence involves dukkha (suffering/unsatisfactoriness), caused by tanha (craving and attachment); ending craving leads to liberation from suffering.
Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
Buddhism teaches that life is nothing but pain and misery.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.

mcqs.q: What is the Eightfold Path in Buddhism?
options: The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
The Eightfold Path is the same as the Four Noble Truths.

The practical path to ending suffering: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration — grouped into wisdom, ethical conduct and mental discipline.
